results_that_do_not_follow.reason: The excess of T1 over its estimate is explained by 9 factorisations instead of 7 (82 s / 9 = 9.1 s), but the same count applied to the present driver gives 9 x 186.45 s = 1678 s, more than the measured t_p of 1456.59 s, so the recorded times do not support 9 full factorisations per solve and the supernodal factor's cost per factorisation (82 s over 7 iterations = 11.7 s against P1's 6.24 s) is left unexplained.

The basis of check D ("P1: 306 fronts split at n = 16, so the parallel path runs") cites a number that is not among the P1 numbers disclosed in lines 65-82, although the section says every number used is disclosed, and no recorded result shows that the parallel path ran in D.

checks_that_cannot_fail.reason: f615_n2_refusals is marked #[ignore], so in this file the N2 assertions (lines 647-663) are never run by the normal test command and cannot fail, while N2 is the only check registered to catch mutations M5 and M6.
assert_eq!(name, en) compares two string literals written in the same file (the got array and EXPECTED), so it passes whatever the solver computed.

assert_eq!(nper - 1, 2 * NC) compares compile-time constants (NTH + 1 = 16 = 2 * 8) and is independent of anything the code under test computes (the same assertion is at line 208 of sa_contact_f615_default_bits.rs).

limits_that_test_nothing.reason: U1's limit of 1e-10 on the displacement (applied at line 582 of sa_contact_supernodal_f615.rs) is four orders of magnitude above the estimate of 7.2e-15 and the measured 7.0e-15, 6.6e-15 and 1.4e-14, so a displacement error several thousand times larger than observed would still pass and the reading limits of V1 and V2 would bind first.
